_what: Seven Days to the Wolves — the whole programme, assembled from its acts. THE RUNNING ORDER IS CANONICAL and settled by the owner on 2026-08-12: intro (I) -> endlessformsmostbeautiful (II) -> mrbobbytables (III) -> kat (IV) -> nat (V) -> 7daystothewolves (VI) -> europa (VII) -> credits (VIII). docs/running-order.md is the source of truth for it; this file executes it.

_acts.0: PROLOGUE -- the main title sequence, and THE ONE ENTRY WITH NO NUMERAL. The eight act numerals are load-bearing (AGENTS.md: 'III is mrbobbytables permanently'), so a cold open in front of act I is numbered outside them rather than by renumbering everything behind it. Like act VIII it carries NO SLIDE AND NO CHAPTER MARKER: chapters() derives markers from slides, and a card announcing the main title sequence would step on the main title sequence. Picture is Nightwish's official 'Perfume Of The Timeless' music video -- see the rights note in music/bed_perfume_of_the_timeless.json, and stories/megacut/delivery.json for why it has no social copy.
_acts.I: intro — the Into the Light opener, six Guardians plated, with the title cover (wolves.jpg) covering source 24.5 - 38.
_acts.II: endlessformsmostbeautiful — delivered and credited, in the programme. Five unbroken runs of the live-action trailers scored to Nightwish's Endless Forms Most Beautiful (instrumental); The Long Walk inside them. See docs/cuts/02-endless-forms-most-beautiful.md. Its picture is a fan compilation (same provenance question as act VI, #55).
_acts.III: mrbobbytables — the August 2026 contributors piece, cut from the Curse of Osiris opening cinematic. Owner-named and owner-placed. He calls it PARTIALLY COMPLETE, so it is placed as-is and will be replaced by its finished version.
_acts.IV: kat — Kat Cosgrove's Guardian intro, behind the owner-authored BIAS FOR ACTION slide.
_acts.V: nat — Natali Vlatko's Guardian arrival, behind the same authorisation slide retitled WRONG PLACE, WRONG TIME, RIGHT ATTITUDE.
_acts.VI: 7daystothewolves — the musical. Editorial pass, delivered for review, not approved: provenance is unresolved (issue #55). Its tail plates the Cayde-6 reveal and three gold credits.
_acts.VIII: credits — the cast, 454 contributors across four projects, the comic-cover reveal at :22 and the Project Bluefin wordmark. The act that makes this the feature rather than seven eighths of it (#51).

_audio: Every act carries its own audio, unprocessed: no normaliser, no limiter, no EQ. The programme is 48 kHz STEREO because that is what the masters are -- every -hq master in Prod is stereo FLAC. The older, now-retired UPLOAD copies were AAC 5.1, but that 5.1 was the same two channels plus a derived LFE (FC/BL/BR digital silence), added by each cut's own run script. Upmixing here to recreate it would be assembly inventing a soundfield, which the audio tenet forbids; if 5.1 delivery is wanted, it belongs in the per-cut scripts that already do it. Only the six act slides are silent; a bed under them is a licensing decision.
_transitions: Issue #105, measured on v0.6 with tools/transitions.py (all times programme clock): every act entered DRY out of the slides' digital silence (4-14 s of -inf per join), the worst being act VII at -15.3 dB one second after the slide, and acts I and III ended HOT against the silence (-24.4 and -14.8 dB in their last second). The treatment below is explicit afade shapes, stated here so they are reproducible: fade_in 2.0 s on every act that starts behind a slide, fade_out 2.0 s on the acts whose tails do not already fade (I, III, V) and 3.0 s on act VII so the programme lands rather than stops. Acts II and VI fade themselves out (measured -96.7 / -90.3 dB in their last seconds) and carry no fade_out; the IV->V join is direct and continuous (-15.2 -> -11.9 dB) and carries no fade on either side. All fade times are ACT FILM time -- the clip's own clock -- so a re-order never moves them. LEFT TO THE OWNER (automatable: no): (1) whether the slides carry a bed or room tone -- a licensing decision, per the megacut skill; (2) levelling the act ENTRIES, which still differ by ~20 dB (act III at -29.5 vs act VII at -15.3) -- static gain per act is a mix decision; (3) how long the slides' silence should be -- the 15 s IV-V slide is deliberate pacing. PROLOGUE JOIN, measured 2026-08-14 on the built act rather than assumed: the prologue's own tail runs -28.3 -> -34.8 -> -58.7 dB RMS across its last three seconds (the song fading under the bridge from 93.000), and act I opens at digital silence (-127 dB) climbing through -30 to -18 dB. So the join needs NO fade on either side and carries none: the prologue fades itself out, exactly as acts II and VI do, and act I's own quiet opening picks it up. A fade_out here would double the taper on a fade the act already performs. ONE EDITORIAL FINDING, LEFT TO THE OWNER (automatable: no): the bridge exists because the owner asked for the wallpaper to 'replace the black part', and act I's 5 s silent slide immediately after it puts a black part back. It reads as a continuous darkening today -- night fades to black and the slide rises out of the same darkness, which is how a title sequence normally hands to act one -- but if the intent was for the wallpaper to hand STRAIGHT into a film, the fix is to drop or restyle act I's slide, and a slide is the one thing this show gives every act. Not changed unilaterally.

They are hardlinks to the per-project masters, so Prod costs no extra disk and cannot drift from what its project built. The retired ~/Videos/UPLOAD staging folder held lossy copies of the same cuts and is NOT what this reads; its removal is issue #81. Act VII's master was re-rendered 2026-08-13 under the new master gate (tools/peaks.py trim, #130) and now measures -1.1 dBTP, inside the -0.9..-1.1 band -- the +0.3 dBTP clip of #82 is fixed in the delivered file; the issue stays open for its owner to close.

items.label: Perfume, movement 5 — source 389.800 -> 507.021 (EOF), Europa into the credits
items._thread: Movement 5 of 5, and the end of the song. The owner: 'match the transition panning up from laura after europa, then hold until the end of this, then roll credits.' Laura Santamaria is Elsie Bray, act VII copy. Act VII's tail is flat at YAVG~37 from 89 s and falls hard over its last half second, so it hands down into this movement's upward move. WHERE EXACTLY THE TWO MOVES MEET IS A CRAFT JUDGEMENT ABOUT FRAMES: this build joins at the measured cut, 389.800, and the frame is for the owner to approve. Act VII is never shortened to make it fit (#178).
items._moves_the_ambush: This changes what act VIII comes out of. The credits carry no slide and no marker because 'Europa fades to black on its own tail and the drum smash lands on the next frame' -- the smash now lands off the end of a DIFFERENT song, and the source's last shot is HELD (luma ~32), not black. The 1.5 s fade_out lets the song land rather than be chopped; the picture is deliberately left un-faded, because these movements are rendered clean for the dinosaur pass and a burned dip would have to be un-baked later. TODO(owner): whether the two pieces of music collide, and whether the ambush wants black in front of it after all.

items.label: Act VIII — Credits
items._what: NO ACT SLIDE, by owner instruction: 'no credits slide, go right to the metal ... it should surprise the viewer.' Every other act is announced by a card; this one is not. Europa fades to black on its own tail and the drum smash lands on the next frame. The missing slide also removes act VIII's CHAPTER MARKER -- chapters() derives them from slides -- and that is the point rather than a side effect: a 'VIII. Credits' entry on the scrub bar would spoil the same surprise the cut is built to land. fade_in is 0.0 so nothing eases in front of the smash.

_chapters: Each act slide carries the audience-facing `chapter` title; `python3 tools/megacut.py <plan> --chapters` derives the timestamps from this plan's own clock, so the markers can never drift from the running order. The numeral is part of the title because the show is told in numbered acts. Act VIII has no film, so it has no marker -- a chapter that jumps to the next act's footage would be a lie about what plays.
_version: v2.0 -- THE PERFUME THREAD. v1.0 was the first build that was the whole feature: all eight acts playing, act VIII (the credits, #51) added with its own slide, and the comic cover cut from the end of act VII (#178) so the reveal happens once, at :22. v2.0 changes the SHAPE of the programme rather than its contents: Nightwish's 'Perfume Of The Timeless' now plays from the first frame to the last frame before the credits, in source order and without gaps, and the eight acts live inside it. Five movements -- the prologue in front of act I, then 93.000->159.400 after act I, 159.400->328.080 after act III, 328.080->389.800 before Europa, and 389.800->EOF from Europa into the credits. None of them takes a numeral, a slide or a chapter marker, so the chapter list still has eight entries, but every timestamp after act I moved. Movements 2-5 add 414.0 s (6:54.0) on top of the prologue's 99.2, taking the feature from 24:07.1 to roughly 32:40. See docs/cuts/00-perfume-thread.md.
